suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-28 adds this relationship only as a bounded mixed-connective-tissue-disease pulmonary-hypertension association. Pulmonary arterial hypertension is reported in mixed connective tissue disease, but the primary diagnosis alone does not establish pulmonary hypertension in every person, its subtype, or an individual's attribution. Require independently documented mixed connective tissue disease and pulmonary hypertension, appropriate cardiopulmonary testing with hemodynamic confirmation when indicated, compatible chronology, and rheumatology/pulmonology review. Preserve interstitial lung disease, thromboembolic disease, left-heart disease, hypoxic lung disease, sleep apnea, infection, and other causes.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of mixed connective tissue disease and separately established pulmonary hypertension with defined subtype

Pulmonology and rheumatology assessment distinguishing pulmonary arterial hypertension from other pulmonary-hypertension phenotypes

sourceReferences.citation: Hassan AB, et al. The prevalence of pulmonary arterial hypertension in patients with mixed connective tissue disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Clin Exp Rheumatol. 2023. PMID 37497727.
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis addressing pulmonary arterial hypertension prevalence in mixed connective tissue disease. It supports a bounded population-level association, not automatic individual causation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 37497727; systematic-review scope and adult mixed-connective-tissue-disease PAH prevalence

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Pulmonary arterial hypertension is reported among people with mixed connective tissue disease, but an individual relationship requires confirmed diagnoses, pulmonary-hypertension subtype, objective testing, chronology, and competing-etiology review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by prevalence evidence; the mapping is not an individual pulmonary-hypertension opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Mixed connective tissue disease may be accompanied by pulmonary vascular or interstitial lung involvement, but the relevant pathway and pulmonary-hypertension subtype must be demonstrated in the individual rather than inferred from the connective-tissue-disease label.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Pulmonary arterial hypertension is a reported complication or comorbidity in mixed connective tissue disease, but prevalence evidence does not establish that the disease caused or aggravated pulmonary hypertension in every individual; subtype, hemodynamics, chronology, treatment, and competing causes require case-specific review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Independent diagnoses and pulmonary-hypertension subtype; objective cardiopulmonary testing; chronology; assessment of ILD, thromboembolic, left-heart, hypoxic, sleep-related, infectious, and other causes; specialist opinion
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Interstitial lung disease, chronic thromboembolic disease, hypoxic lung disease, or sleep apnea
Left-heart disease, valvular disease, congenital heart disease, or another cardiopulmonary disorder
Medication, infection, vasculitis, idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension, or other vascular causes
